info.name: Smart E-Commerce Platform API
info.description:
Generated from the OpenAPI schema by tools/generate_postman.py.

1. Set `base_url` (default http://127.0.0.1:8000).
2. Run **Authentication → Login**; it stores the tokens automatically.
3. Every other request inherits Bearer auth from the collection.

WebSockets can't be represented here: connect a WS client to {{base_url}}/ws/notifications?token={{access_token}}.

query.description: Size of the revenue/orders trend window.

request.description:
Everything the analytics dashboard shows, in one call.

Revenue counts only settled (succeeded) payments. Units sold and category
sales exclude cancelled orders. All timestamps are UTC.
Every outgoing email and whether it was delivered.
Re-send an email that failed over SMTP.

query.description: Only active or only deactivated accounts.

request.description:
Every account with its order count and lifetime spend.

Read-only by design: roles are changed directly in MySQL
(`UPDATE users SET role = 'staff' WHERE id = ...`).

exec: // Save the tokens so every other request in this collection is authorised.

request.description: Revoke a refresh token (the access token simply expires).

Validate cart -> create order + payment record -> initialize payment.

payment_method=stripe -> Stripe Checkout Session (flow=session, returns
    checkout_url) or PaymentIntent (flow=intent, returns client_secret)
payment_method=cash   -> cash on delivery; a CASH-... transaction id is
    issued immediately and staff/admin confirm receipt on delivery via
    POST /payments/cash/confirm/{order_id}

Your inbox: every email the store sent you, newest first.

A copy of each email is always kept here, so this works even when your
address can't receive mail (a made-up address on a local account, or no
mail server configured).

Mark emails as read: `{"email_ids": [4, 5]}`, or `{"all": true}` / an empty body for all.

Only your own emails are touched. Your other open tabs get an
`emails_read` WebSocket event so their unread badge updates too.
Unread count for the inbox badge, and how mail to your address is delivered.
One email sent to you. Reading it doesn't mark it read — use POST /dev/emails/read.
Admin only: the platform's role definitions.

The signed-in user's notifications, newest first.

Types: `order_placed`, `order_confirmed`, `payment_successful`,
`payment_failed`, `order_shipped`, `order_delivered`, `order_cancelled`.

Mark notifications as read.

* `{"notification_ids": [12, 13]}` — just those
* `{"all": true}` or an empty body — every unread notification

Only ever touches the caller's own notifications; ids belonging to someone
else are ignored. Other open tabs get a `notifications_read` WebSocket
event so their unread badge updates too.
Staff/admin: every customer's orders, with customer identity.

Admin only: delete an order with its items, payment, and invoice.
Reserved stock is returned to products unless the order already shipped.

Ask to send an order back.

Allowed only on your own order, once it has been **delivered**, and within
the return window (RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, 7 by default). One open request per
order: the order moves to `return_requested` until staff approve or reject
it, and approving issues the refund.

query.description:
The new order status — pick one from the list. Which values are actually accepted depends on where the order is now:

* **pending** → `cancelled` (to mark it paid, confirm the payment instead: POST /payments/confirm/{order_id})
* **paid** → `shipped` or `cancelled`
* **shipped** → `delivered` or `cancelled`
* **delivered** / **cancelled** → final, nothing further

GET /orders/{order_id}/status-options tells you the answer for one specific order.

request.description:
Move an order along its lifecycle (staff/admin).

`pending → paid → shipped → delivered`, and `cancelled` from any stage
before delivery. An order never reaches **paid** here — that happens by
confirming its payment, which also settles the payment record and issues
the invoice.

What can I do with this order right now?

Ask this before calling the status endpoint and you never have to guess:
it returns the order's current status and exactly which values
`PUT /orders/{order_id}/status` will accept for it, plus whether the
payment can still be confirmed.

Staff/admin confirm cash was received on delivery -> order paid + invoice.

Same as POST /payments/confirm/{order_id} but refuses anything that isn't a
cash-on-delivery payment, so the "cash received" action can't be used by
mistake on a card order that hasn't actually been paid.

Staff/admin: confirm (or fail) an order's payment by order id.

Marks the payment succeeded, moves the order to `paid`, issues the invoice
and notifies the customer — the same path the Stripe webhook takes, so a
manually confirmed order ends up in exactly the same state as an
automatically confirmed one. Works for Stripe and cash alike.

query.description: Stripe checkout session id, as handed back on the success redirect.
Look the receipt up by order instead.

request.description:
The receipt for a completed checkout — what the success page renders.

Stripe redirects the shopper to {CHECKOUT_SUCCESS_URL}?session_id=... after
payment; the page passes that straight here. Customers can only read their
own receipts; staff and admin can read anyone's.

Stripe webhook: point your Stripe dashboard endpoint at POST /payments/webhook.

Handles checkout.session.completed and payment_intent.succeeded/failed.
Admin only: delete a payment record. The order reverts to payment pending.
Alias of GET /returns/all. Staff/admin: every return request.
Your own return requests, newest first.
Staff/admin: every return request. `?status=pending` is the work queue.
The reasons a customer may choose, for the storefront's dropdown.

Staff/admin: approve a return, refund the payment, restock the items.

The refund goes through Stripe for live card payments; cash, mock-mode
and anything Stripe can't refund get a local reference so the money still
has an audit trail. The customer is notified and emailed either way.
Staff/admin: decline a return. The order goes back to delivered.
